skill.name: reverse-engineer-anything
skill.description: Guide REA investigations of shipped applications, binaries, packages, and runtime behavior, and build recorded web or Linux desktop agent environments.
skill.summary: Investigate application artifacts with evidence-linked REA workflows and create agent environments from recorded behavior.
skill.author: morluto

security_audit.summary: All 305 static alerts are false positives involving Markdown, documentation, scoped application state, or legitimate configuration. Three semantic risks concern unisolated runtime execution, incomplete credential redaction, and default paid measurement in headless builds. No evidence found of malicious exfiltration or prompt injection in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Native runtime workflows can execute targets with host-user permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Require a disposable, isolated host for untrusted native targets. Explain filesystem and network exposure before launch or debugger attachment.

remediation.issue: Capture redaction does not protect all credentials in recorded responses.
remediation.suggestion: Use disposable credentials, declare secrets before recording, and mark saved tokens secret. Require a credential review before retaining or exporting captures.

remediation.issue: Headless builds permit paid measurement without an explicit request.
remediation.suggestion: Default unattended builds to skipping measurement. Require explicit authorization for model calls, the endpoint, and a total budget.

content.user_title: Reverse Engineer Applications With REA Evidence
content.value_statement: Shipped applications can hide behavior that source inspection alone cannot establish. This skill guides REA artifact analysis, runtime observation, and recorded agent environment creation.
actual_capabilities: Route native binaries, managed assemblies, Android APKs, firmware, and application packages to relevant REA analysis tools.
Guide static analysis of Electron and JavaScript applications, feature tracing, and application version comparisons.
Guide scoped browser, Electron, debugger, instrumentation, and process observation with explicit target and cleanup boundaries.
Reuse retained evidence, inspect selected result pages, and export investigation bundles with coverage and unknowns.
Build web agent environments from browser scenarios or retained traffic captures and report supported read and write behavior.
Build Linux desktop environments with synthetic seeds, task checks, fresh-computer verification, and optional model-based measurement.
limitations: Installing the skill alone does not install REA, register its MCP server, or supply required analysis engines.
Tool availability depends on the connected REA version, operating system, and caller-supplied prerequisites.
Static findings and decompiler output do not prove runtime behavior, original source recovery, or complete application equivalence.
Runtime execution is not host isolation, captures can retain sensitive data, and model-based evaluation can incur charges.

use_cases.title: Review Shipped Application Exposure
use_cases.description: Inspect a selected release package for recoverable code, resources, and exposure evidence while preserving unassessed checks and limitations.

use_cases.title: Investigate Release Differences
use_cases.description: Compare two supplied application versions and trace a changed feature through static evidence, adding authorized runtime observations when needed.

use_cases.title: Create Agent Evaluation Environments
use_cases.description: Record disposable web application behavior or build synthetic Linux desktop tasks with repeatable checks and fresh-environment verification.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Supplied Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [artifact path] with available REA static tools. Summarize its structure, identity, limitations, and unanswered questions. Do not execute the target.

prompt_templates.title: Trace an Electron Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [ASAR or extracted application path] with REA. Trace [feature] through relevant modules and IPC relationships. Cite evidence and distinguish inferred links from observations.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Application Releases
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [old artifact path] and [new artifact path] for [feature]. Reuse compatible evidence and explain changed, unchanged, and unknown behavior. Do not execute either target.

prompt_templates.title: Build and Verify a Desktop Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Linux desktop environment for [application] with the task [requested edit]. Use synthetic data and verify checks against seed, correct edit, near miss, and reset. Export locally to [directory]. Do not run paid measurement or screen judging without my explicit approval.

output_examples.input: Trace how a supplied Electron application handles its export command without running it.
output: The report identifies the supplied artifact and the modules associated with the export command.
A uniquely matched literal IPC channel supports an inferred link between renderer and main-process handlers.
Dynamic destinations and actual runtime execution remain unknown until separately observed.

output_examples.input: Build an Inkscape environment where an agent changes a synthetic poster headline and saves it.
output: The local bundle contains a synthetic poster seed and a task describing the requested headline change.
The verification report records failures on the seed and near miss, success after the correct edit, and failure after reset.
The handoff lists the bundle location, checks, recording locations, limitations, and whether paid measurement was authorized.

best_practices: Select explicit targets and use the smallest static evidence workflow that answers the question before requesting runtime execution.
Use disposable environments and synthetic data; review captured credentials and seed files before exporting or sharing.
Preserve artifact identities, evidence references, coverage limits, and unknowns; approve model endpoints and budgets before paid evaluation.
anti_patterns: Run untrusted native targets on a sensitive host or treat observation paths as a security sandbox.
Treat recovered pseudocode, inferred links, or partial inventories as proof of original source or complete runtime behavior.
Record production writes, share unreviewed captures, or accept unattended model charges without explicit authorization.

faq.question: Does installing this skill install REA?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides instructions. A separate REA installation and connection are required unless a client plugin already supplies them.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Available REA operations still depend on the connected server and host prerequisites.

faq.question: Can it recover the original source code?
faq.answer: Not generally. It guides supported decompilation and source recovery workflows, but recovered representations do not guarantee the original source.

faq.question: Does artifact inspection execute the application?
faq.answer: Static inspection workflows do not execute the target. Runtime workflows can launch, attach to, or modify selected targets and require separate scope decisions.

faq.question: Are exported captures guaranteed to exclude secrets?
faq.answer: No. Redaction has documented gaps, and exports retain recorded data. Use disposable credentials and review captures before exporting or sharing.

faq.question: Do desktop tasks require paid model evaluation?
faq.answer: Not all tasks do. Measurement and screen judging use configured model services; the headless build default permits measurement unless explicitly disabled.
